input.story: As a registered user, I want to manage my profile, change my password, set up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, see and revoke my active sessions, link my Google or GitHub account, choose light or dark theme with auto-saving, upload an avatar up to 5 MB, and permanently delete my account, so that my account is accurate and secure.

criteria.text: The profile page shows the full name, email, phone number and bio
Changing the password requires the current password
Enabling two-factor shows a 6-digit verification code step
An avatar must be a JPEG, PNG or WebP image under 5MB
Active sessions list each device and can be revoked
Deleting the account asks for the password again

test_cases.title: The profile page shows every field
steps: Open the profile page
test_cases.expected: The page shows the full name, email, phone number and bio

test_cases.title: Changing the password asks for the current one
steps: Open the password form
Submit without the current password
test_cases.expected: The form shows: Enter your current password

test_cases.title: Enabling two-factor asks for a 6-digit code
steps: Open security settings
Press Enable two-factor
test_cases.expected: The page asks for a 6-digit verification code

problems.says: Unlinking the last sign-in method is blocked: Removing the last way to sign in locks the owner out with one click.
Length boundary: one below the minimum and exactly the minimum: One character out and you either refuse a good password or accept a short one.
Other sessions are signed out after the change: People change a password after a theft. If the thief stays signed in, it was pointless.
The password never appears in a URL, log or error message: A password in the web address is saved in history, in logs and in screenshots.
HTML or script in the bio is shown as text: Other people see this text. If it is not escaped, their browser runs it.
A revoked session's token is refused by the API immediately: If the list says signed out but the device still works, nothing was signed out.
A wrong code is rejected: If a wrong code is ever accepted, the second step protects nobody.
An expired code is rejected: A code that still works ten minutes later is just a password someone can read and reuse.
The same code cannot be used twice: If the same code works twice, anyone who sees it once can sign in again.
A recovery code works once and only once: People write backup codes on paper and photograph them. One that works twice is a spare key for life.
AC-4 has no tests yet.
problems.fix: Write at least one test that covers AC-4.

problems.says: AC-5 has no tests yet.
problems.fix: Write at least one test that covers AC-5.

problems.says: AC-6 has no tests yet.
problems.fix: Write at least one test that covers AC-6.

problems.says: An empty (0-byte) file: An empty file is under every size limit. It then breaks whatever tries to read it.
An image with very large dimensions: A small image file can open into a huge one. The server runs out of memory resizing it.
The network drops during the upload: Uploads from a phone often stop half way. The page must say so, not look finished.
The user cancels at the provider's consent screen: Cancel is the most pressed button on that screen, and it usually lands on an error page.
A provider error or timeout is handled: That server belongs to someone else. When it is slow or fails, the user still needs somewhere to land.
A new password equal to the old one is rejected: Saving the same password again looks like a change. The old, leaked one still works.
A confirmation that does not match blocks the save: A typo here, in text nobody checks, can lock the owner out of their own account.
Rapid toggles end on the last chosen value: Auto-save sends one request per click. The answers come back in any order.
A failed save shows an error and puts the toggle back: If the save failed but the switch stays on, the user believes something that is not true.
The setting survives a reload and appears on another device: A setting saved only in this browser looks saved. It is gone on the next computer.
Each field at its limit and one character over: If only the page checks the length, the server saves a cut-off value or fails.
Phone numbers with +, spaces, and one that is too short: Everyone writes phone numbers differently. A strict field rejects real ones; a loose one keeps rubbish.
The same profile edited in two tabs — the last save does not silently overwrite: People work in two tabs. Losing one tab's work without a word is lost data.
TC-01: fewer than 2 steps
problems.fix: Rewrite it so the expected result can only be true or false, and say the exact values it uses.

problems.says: TC-02: the steps enter data but no test data is given
problems.fix: Rewrite it so the expected result can only be true or false, and say the exact values it uses.

problems.says: AC-1 has only one test.
problems.fix: Add a second test for AC-1.

problems.says: AC-2 has only one test.
problems.fix: Add a second test for AC-2.

problems.says: AC-3 has only one test, no test for wrong input, no test at the limits.
problems.fix: Add a second test, a test for wrong input, a test at the limit, using the exact value for AC-3.

problems.says: Cancelling during the upload: People stop an upload half way. A half-written file left behind becomes a support ticket.
The theme applies without a page reload and reads in both modes: People see the theme first. Needing a reload, or grey on grey, is the first thing they notice.
Leaving with unsaved changes warns first: Typing a long answer and losing it to one stray click is what people complain about.
The session list shows the device and when it was last active: If every row looks the same, nobody knows which one to sign out.

add_tests.title: Deleting the account asks for the password before it starts
steps: Open the delete-account flow and reach the confirmation step
Submit it with a wrong password
Submit it again with the correct password
add_tests.expected: The wrong password leaves the account untouched and shows an error; the correct password starts the deletion and the step is recorded.

add_tests.title: The deleted account's password no longer signs anyone in
steps: Try to sign in with the deleted account's email and password
Try the password reset flow with the same email
Try to sign in with the provider that was linked to it
add_tests.expected: All three are refused, the message is the same one an unknown email gets, and no session is created.

add_tests.title: Every session and API token of a deleted account stops working
steps: Complete the deletion from browser A
Reload a protected page in browser B
Call a protected API endpoint with the captured token
add_tests.expected: Browser B is sent to the sign-in page and the API answers 401 for the captured token; neither keeps working after the deletion.
add_tests.test_data: two browser sessions and one captured API token for user@example.com

add_tests.title: A file at the size limit uploads and one byte over is refused
steps: Upload an image of exactly the stated limit
Upload the same image with one extra byte
Upload a file a little under the limit
add_tests.expected: The exact-limit file and the smaller file upload and appear; the one-byte-over file is refused with a message naming the limit, and the previous avatar is unchanged.
add_tests.test_data: three JPEG files: limit minus 1 KB, exactly the limit, limit plus 1 byte

add_tests.title: An executable renamed to .jpg is refused
steps: Upload avatar.jpg, which is really a non-image file
Upload a text file renamed to photo.png
Upload a real JPEG to confirm the happy path still works
add_tests.expected: Both disguised files are refused with a message about the file type, nothing is written to storage, and the real JPEG still uploads.

add_tests.title: Signing in with a provider whose email matches an existing password account
steps: Sign out and press Continue with Google
Complete the provider sign-in with user@example.com
Open the account's sign-in methods afterwards
add_tests.expected: The product follows one stated rule — either it asks for the password before linking, or it refuses — and never ends with two accounts for user@example.com or data from one account visible in the other.
add_tests.test_data: email=user@example.com on both the password account and the provider account

add_tests.title: Boundary values at 5 digits / 7 digits (AC-3)
steps: Reach 5-digit.
Reach 7-digit.
Check the result.
add_tests.expected: At 5 digits: AC-3 still holds at 5 digits. 7 digits is past the limit AC-3 states, so it is refused.

add_tests.title: Boundary values at 4.99 MB / 5 MB / 5.01 MB (AC-4)
steps: Reach 4.99MB.
Reach 5MB.
Reach 5.01MB.
Check the result.
add_tests.expected: At 4.99 MB: AC-4 still holds at 4.99 MB. 5 MB is refused: AC-4 says "under 5MB". 5.01 MB is past the limit AC-4 states, so it is refused.
